But that's not drama. Science MEASURED it.
In 2016, UCL scientists gave 45 people a game with mild electric SHOCKS.

Think of the last chat you REFRESHED. Yeah. That one.

post.title: Why Waiting for a Text Feels Worse Than a No #shorts
post.description: Send this to the friend still staring at "typing…" Sam sent the text. "Read 9:14." An hour later he'd honestly rather get a no. That isn't drama. In a 2016 Nature Communications study, Archy de Berker, Sven Bestmann and colleagues at University College London had 45 volunteers play a game of turning over rocks that might hide a snake, and a snake meant a mildly painful electric shock. Stress (pupil dilation, sweating and how stressed people said they felt) was highest when the chance of a shock was about 50%, and lowest when it was 0% or 100%: a sure shock was less stressful than a maybe. Uncertainty itself is stressful, because your brain keeps trying to predict what happens next. Not knowing is the stress. Comment 'got me' if you've stared at 'Read' too. #psychology #shorts #overthinking #anxiety #texting
